sentences.text: .2. The brief facts of the case is that the land bearing Sy.No. 25/2 measuring 32 guntas of Byalalu village, Tavarakere Hobli, Bengaluru South Taluka has been acquired for construction of houses.
Preliminary notification was issued on 19.03.2011.
The final notification has been published in the Gazette on 27.11.2012.
The L.A.O. has passed the award on 02.09.2015.
The L.A.O. has fixed the compensation of Rs.85,75,463/-.
As O.S.No. 585/2013 was pending for adjudication, the L.A.O. has referred the matter to this Court and has deposited a sum of Rs. 85,75,463/-.
The said amount has been kept in FD in the Canara Bank, KLE Society Branch, Rajajinagara, Bengaluru.
.3. After receipt of reference, this court issued notices to claimant and the objectors.
They have entered appearance and have filed claim statement.

.4. Claimant - Munihanumaiah has filed claim statement stating that the property bearing Sy.No.
25/2 measuring 32 guntas in Byalalu village, Tavarekere Hobli, Bengaluru South Taluka was owned and possessed by Chikkamuniyaiah and he being the owner was in possession and enjoyment of the same.
The said Chikkamuniyaiah and his wife Puttamma died by leaving 3 sons by name Puttahanumaiah, Channahanumaiah and Motappaiah.
Puttahanumaiah died intestate by leaving Munihanumaiah and Hanumakka as his legal heirs to succeed to his estate.

Sri. Channahanumaiah died intestate by leaving Munihanumaiah, Ramakrishna, Muniraju, Marakka and Nagamma as his legal heirs to succeed to his estate and Sri.Motappaiah and his wife Revamma died intestate by leaving Chikkamuniyappa, Munihanumaiah, Somaiah and Hanumaiah as his legal heirs to succeed to his estate.
One of the son of Mottappaiah by name Somaiah died intestate by leaving his wife Hanumakka and children Manjunath, Chandru and Smt. Chaya to succeed to his estate.
It is stated that all the revenue records in-respect of Sy.No. 25/2 measuring 32 guntas was standing in the name of Chikkamuniyaiah.

After the death of Chikkamuniyaiah all the revenue records are changed in the name of his eldest son Puttahanumaiah as per the oral partition between Puttahanumaiah,
Channahanumaiah and Mottappaiah.

It is stated that the children of Mottappaiah had filed a suit in O.S.No. 585/2013 against Munihanumaiah who is the claimant in the above case and also against his wife and children pending on the file of Prl. Senior Civil Judge and CJM at Ramanagara for partition and separate possession.
It is stated that the above said suit came to be transferred after the establishment of Senior Civil Judge Court at Magadi and re-numbered as O.S.No. 702/2014.

sentences.text: The above said referred suit in O.S.No. 702/2014 was got dismissed as not pressed in view of the memo filed by the plaintiffs by order dated 27.09.2021.
It is stated that the claimant is the only person who is entitled to the entire award amount with accrued interest.
Hence, prayed for disbursement of compensation amount.
.6. The claimants 1 to 16 have filed memo stating that they have no objection to disburse the award amount with accrued interest thereon with all consequential benefits in-favour of claimant.
.7. The claimants 4, 5, 6(a) to 6(d), 7 to 9 have filed memo stating that the compensation amount may be paid to claimant No. 1.
The claimant No. 3 has stated he has no claim and no objection to disburse the compensation in-favour of the claimants.
.8. The claimants 11,13 and 15 have appeared before Court and have submitted that they have no claim and compensation may be paid to claimant No. 1.

objector No. 12 which should be claimant No. 12 has stated that award may be passed in-favour of claimant No. 1.
.9.

The claimant No. 16 Munihanumaiah has filed claim statement stating that Sy.No. 25/2 measuring 32 guntas situated at Byalalu village, Tavarekere Hobli, is his ancestral property and he is one of the Co-owner of the said property and there is no any family partition at any time.
It is stated that late. Sri. Channahanumaiah is his father.
That his father late. Channahanumaiah died leaving behind him and his younger brothers claimants 8 and 9, he is entitled to get the legitimate share on compensation amount as joint family member.

Subsequently memo filed he has no objection to disburse the compensation amount in- favour of claimant No. 1.
.10.
The claimant No. 1 is Special Power of Attorney holder of claimant No. 10 and no claim statement is filed on her behalf.
.11. In order to prove their case, the claimant Munihanumaiah is examined as PW.1.
One Umeshchandra is examined as PW.2.

The documents got marked at Ex.P.1 to P.20.
.11.
Heard the arguments.

.12. The following points that would arise for my consideration are:
1) Which of the claimant and objectors are entitled to receive the compensation amount?

Point No.1 : As per discussion Point No.2 : As per final order, for the following:
REASONS .14. POINT No.1 : The claimant Munihanumaiah has been examined as PW.1.
He has stated that the land bearing Sy.No. 25/2 measuring 32 guntas of Byalalu village was owned and possessed by Chikkamuniyaiah.
He had 3 sons by name Puttahanumaiah, Channahanumaiah and Motappaiah.
PW. 1 has stated that all of them died intestate leaving behind the legal heirs to succeed to his estate.

Channahanumaiah died intestate by leaving Munihanumaiah (claimant No. 5),
Ramakrishna ( claimant No. 8), Muniraju ( claimant No. 9), Marakka and Nagamma as his legal heirs to succeed to his estate.

Motappaiah and his wife Revamma died intestate by leaving Chikkamuniyappa (claimant No. 4), Munihanumaiah (claimant),
Somaiah ( claimant No. 6) and Hanumaiah ( claimant No. 7) as his legal heirs to succeed to his estate.

The claimant No. 6 died leaving behind his legal heirs i.e.,
claimant No. 6(a) to 6(d).
.15.
PW.1 has stated that all the revenue records in-respect of Sy.No. 25/2 measuring 32 guntas was standing in the name of Chikkamuniyaiah.

After the death of Chikkamuniyaiah all the revenue records are changed in the name of his eldest son Puttahanumaiah as per the oral partition between Puttahanumaiah,
Channahanumaiah and Mottappaiah.
After the death of Puttahanumaiah all the revenue records changed in his name.
.16. To corroborate his contention, PW. 1 has produced Genealogical tree as per Ex.P.1
From the document it is seen that the claimant is the son of Puttahanumaiah and Rudramuniyamma.

Ex.P.18 is the mutation in-respect of MR No. 15/2013-14,
wherein name of claimant has been entered in-respect of Sy.No. 25/2.

Ex.P.2 is the mutation which discloses that katha stood in the name of Puttahanumaiah and in view of his death and death of his wife Rudramuniyamma, Katha has been changed to the name of their son- Munihanumaiah.
Ex.P.3 is three RTC Extracts in- respect of Sy.No. 25/2 for the period from 1976 to 91.
In all these documents also the name of Puttahanumaiah has been entered to an extent of 1.25 guntas and in Col. No. 10 it is mentioned as Pitrajitha.

Ex.P.4 is 21 RTC Extracts for the period from 2001 to 2021,
wherein name of Munihanumaiah has been mentioned in pursuance to IHC No.
4/98-99 in-respect of 1.25 guntas.
Ex.P.5 is the nil Encumbrance certificate issued by the Tahsildar, Bengaluru South in- respect of Sy.No. 25/2.
Ex.P.6 is nil encumbrance from 01.04.2004 to 2021 in-respect of Sy.No. 25/2.
Ex.P.7 and 8 is nil encumbrance from 01.08.1986 to 31.05.1989 and 01.06.89 to 31.03.2004 respectively.
Ex.P.20 is nil encumbrance for the period from 01.04.1950 to 31.07.1986 in-respect of Sy.No. 25/2 measuring 1.25 guntas.
Ex.P.9 is the Aakar bandh.

.17. PW. 1 has stated that children of Mottappaiah had filed O.S.No. 585/2013 against him and his wife and children before the Prl. Senior Civil Judge and CJM at Ramanagara for partition and separate possession.

sentences.text: The said suit has been dismissed as not pressed in view of the memo filed by the plaintiff in that case.
In support of his contention he has produced the order sheet in O.S.No. 702/2014 as per Ex.P14.
From the order sheet it is seen that suit has been dismissed on 27.09.2021.
PW.1 has stated that in view of dismissal of the suit and in view of revenue records standing in his name, he is the only person entitled to receive entire award amount with accrued interest thereon.
.18. During cross-examination PW. 1 has stated that Munihanumaiah is his junior uncle's son.
He admits that his junior uncle is entitled for 11  guntas in L.A.C. No. 46/2020 and in pursuance to the settlement he is entitled for entire amount of compensation in this case.
He admits that he has no objections for his junior uncle's son to receive the compensation in-respect of said 11  guntas.
PW.1 admits that in the notification the name of Munihanumaiah S/o Chikkamuniyaiah has been mentioned.
He has stated that Chikkamuniyaiah is his grand father.
He has stated that during the life time of his father, there is no division among family members, recently they have partitioned the property.
He admits that he has requested the respondent to pay compensation, but he has not produced any documents.

It is elicited that he has 8 children namely Gangahanumakka, Puttamma,
Sharadamma, Hanumantharaju, Rudramuniyappa, Gowramma, Munirathna and Lokesh.
He admits that he and his children have not partitioned the property.
.19. One Umeshchandra is examined as PW.2.
He has stated that he has no claim in-respect of acquired land and the compensation may be paid to claimant No. 1.

.20. From the oral and documentary evidence, it is clear that Sy.No. 25/2 is ancestral property and the claimants 2 to 16 have filed memo stating that they have no objections to release the compensation amount in favour of claimant No.1.
From the evidence, it is seen that claimant No.1 has got 8 children who have all attained majority.
As the property is ancestral property, the claimant No.1 and his children are together entitled for compensation amount.
Hence, point No. 1 is answered partly in the affirmative.
.21. POINT NO.2:

In view of my finding on point No.1, I proceed to pass the following:

Claimant No.1 - Munihanumaiah and his 8 children namely Gangahanumakka,
Puttamma,Sharadamma,Hanumantharaju, Rudramuniyappa, Gowramma,
Munirathna and Lokesh are together entitled for compensation in-respect of Sy.No.
25/2 measuring 32 guntas of Byalalu village, Tavarekere Hobli, Bengaluru South Taluka with accrued interest thereon.

The above claimants shall have to execute indemnity bonds with one surety,
undertaking to re-deposit the compensation amount either in this court or in any other court, if ordered to do so, which amount they are going to receive in this case.
The above claimants are entitled to interest under Section 80 of L.A. Act.
The amount already paid by L.A.O., has to be deducted.
Claim in-respect of claimants 2 to 16 is dismissed.
Draw award accordingly.

 The Special Land Acquisition Officer,
 Karnataka Housing Board,
 Bengaluru - 560 009.
 (Sri. DBG, Advocate)
 5 L.A.C. No.271/2019  : JUDGMENT :
The respondent/SLAO, Karnataka Housing Board, Bengaluru, has made this reference under Section 77(1) of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (hereinafter referred to as 'RFCTLA Act' for short) for apportionment of compensation amount.
Preliminary notification was issued on 19.03.2011.
The final notification has been published in the Gazette on 27.11.2012.
opennyai_summary.facts:
The L.A.O. has passed the award on 02.09.2015.
The L.A.O. has fixed the compensation of Rs.85,75,463/-.
The said Chikkamuniyaiah and his wife Puttamma died by leaving 3 sons by name Puttahanumaiah, Channahanumaiah and Motappaiah.
Puttahanumaiah died intestate by leaving Munihanumaiah and Hanumakka as his legal heirs to succeed to his estate.
Sri. Channahanumaiah died intestate by leaving Munihanumaiah, Ramakrishna, Muniraju, Marakka and Nagamma as his legal heirs to succeed to his estate and Sri.Motappaiah and his wife Revamma died intestate by leaving Chikkamuniyappa, Munihanumaiah, Somaiah and Hanumaiah as his legal heirs to succeed to his estate.
One of the son of Mottappaiah by name Somaiah died intestate by leaving his wife Hanumakka and children Manjunath, Chandru and Smt. Chaya to succeed to his estate.
Hence, prayed for disbursement of compensation amount.
.6. The claimants 1 to 16 have filed memo stating that they have no objection to disburse the award amount with accrued interest thereon with all consequential benefits in-favour of claimant.
The claimant No. 3 has stated he has no claim and no objection to disburse the compensation in-favour of the claimants.
opennyai_summary.issue:
.12. The following points that would arise for my consideration are:
1) Which of the claimant and objectors are entitled to receive the compensation amount?
Sri. Munihanumaiah vs The Special Land Acquisition Officer on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199513440/
5 2)
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
He has stated that he has no claim in-respect of acquired land and the compensation may be paid to claimant No. 1.
From the evidence, it is seen that claimant No.1 has got 8 children who have all attained majority.
As the property is ancestral property, the claimant No.1 and his children are together entitled for compensation amount.
opennyai_summary.decision:
.21. POINT NO.2:
The reference made by the respondent/SLAO under Section 77(1) of the Right to Fair compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act 2013 is partly allowed.
Claimant No.1 - Munihanumaiah and his 8 children namely Gangahanumakka,
Puttamma,Sharadamma,Hanumantharaju, Rudramuniyappa, Gowramma,
Munirathna and Lokesh are together entitled for compensation in-respect of Sy.No.
25/2 measuring 32 guntas of Byalalu village, Tavarekere Hobli, Bengaluru South Taluka with accrued interest thereon.
The above claimants shall have to execute indemnity bonds with one surety,
undertaking to re-deposit the compensation amount either in this court or in any other court, if ordered to do so, which amount they are going to receive in this case.
The above claimants are entitled to interest under Section 80 of L.A. Act.
The amount already paid by L.A.O., has to be deducted.
Claim in-respect of claimants 2 to 16 is dismissed.
Draw award accordingly.
